name: Kelp
rootCause: DPRK breached LayerZero's infrastructure, forged a bridge message, and walked $290 million out of KelpDAO in one transaction. Aave is holding hundreds of millions in bad debt. The dominoes are still falling. DeFi United is scrambling to catch them.

descriptions.text: DPRK breached LayerZero's infrastructure, forged a bridge message, and walked $290 million out of KelpDAO in one transaction. Aave is holding hundreds of millions in bad debt. The dominoes are still falling. DeFi United is scrambling to catch them.

The KelpDAO exploit, attributed to North Korea's Lazarus Group (DPRK TraderTraitor / UNC4899), was an infrastructure-level attack rather than a smart-contract bug. The attackers social-engineered a LayerZero Labs developer to harvest internal session credentials, pivoted into LayerZero's cloud RPC environment, and poisoned two internal RPC nodes to return attacker-controlled chain state. A simultaneous DDoS against the external RPC nodes forced the sole LayerZero DVN — KelpDAO had deployed a critically fragile 1-of-1 DVN configuration with LayerZero Labs as the only required verifier — to fail over exclusively to the poisoned nodes. The compromised nodes fabricated rsETH burn events on the Unichain source chain that never occurred; the DVN attested to these phantom messages, and the Ethereum-side bridge contract duly released 116,500 rsETH (~$292M) to attacker-controlled addresses without any corresponding collateral destruction. The stolen rsETH was deposited into Aave V3, Compound V3, and Euler as collateral to borrow ~$228M in WETH and wstETH. KelpDAO's emergency pause, executed 46 minutes after the drain began, blocked follow-up transactions that would have released an additional ~$200M. LayerZero subsequently banned all 1-of-1 DVN configurations. Attack Tx: 0x1ae232da212c45f35c1525f851e4c41d529bf18af862d9ce9fd40bf709db4222 Analysis: Explained: The Kelp DAO Hack (April 2026) — Halborn Inside the KelpDAO Bridge Exploit — Chainalysis Phalcon_xyz on X

LayerZero issued a statement saying that on April 18, Kelp DAO suffered an attack resulting in approximately $290 million in losses. The incident is initially assessed to have been carried out by a highly sophisticated nation-state actor, suspected to be the TraderTraitor subgroup of North Korea’s Lazarus Group. The attack was completely isolated to Kelp DAO’s rsETH configuration and was caused by its use of a single DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network) setup. The LayerZero protocol itself was not exploited, and no other cross-chain assets or applications were affected. The core of the attack involved the hacker compromising downstream RPC infrastructure used by LayerZero’s DVN.…

Kelp DAO's rsETH bridge lost 116,500 rsETH, about $292 million, after a forged LayerZero packet passed a single-DVN path; Arbitrum later froze 30,766 ETH linked to the exploit. A forged LayerZero packet cleared Kelp's Unichain to Ethereum route because the bridge trusted a single required DVN, and LayerZero's verification pipeline had been compromised upstream. Public reporting still disagrees on whether the 1-of-1 setup was Kelp's deployment choice or LayerZero's default configuration.

On April 18, 2026, KelpDAO's rsETH bridge lost approximately $292M after an attacker compromised off-chain RPC infrastructure supporting its LayerZero single-verifier configuration. The forged message led to a release of real rsETH on Ethereum, triggering cross-chain market freezes and partial recovery actions. The exploit occurred because KelpDAO's rsETH LayerZero bridge was configured with only one Decentralized Verifier Network (DVN) , LayerZero Labs as sole verifier. The attacker compromised the DVN's downstream RPC nodes, forcing it to attest to a fabricated cross-chain message and release 116,500 rsETH without a corresponding event on the source chain.

An attacker stole 116,500 rsETH ( restaked ether) from a blockchain bridge run by Kelp DAO. Based on prices at the time of the theft, the stolen tokens would be worth around $292 million — however, the attacker is likely to face challenges selling a quantity of tokens that amounts to 18% of rsETH's circulating supply. When tokens are bridged from one chain to another, the tokens on the original chain are locked in the bridge smart contract while the token is used on the other chain, preventing its owner from double-spending the asset. With 116,500 locked rsETH now stolen, those using the token on other blockchains are now holding possibly unbacked tokens.…
